$comment: A scoop manifest, and the easiest of the five packaging targets by a long way.
No account, no review, no signing: a JSON file in a bucket pointing at a release
asset and its hash. That is why it is first in docs/packaging.md, and why this
file exists before any of the others: it proves the release SHAPE is right
before anything harder depends on it.
TO PUBLISH: put this in a bucket repository as bucket/atrium.json, with version
and hash filled in from scripts/release.sh output, then:
UNVERIFIED. This has never been installed. It is written from scoop's schema
and the URL it names does not exist yet, because nothing has been released.
autoupdate is what makes a bucket worth having: scoop rewrites version, url
and hash itself when a new tag appears, so publishing a release becomes one
commit rather than three edits somebody gets wrong.
description: Organizes coding agents. A daemon with durable state, a permission gate, a web board, and a pseudo terminal per runner you can attach to from a browser.
notes: Nothing starts on its own. `atrium daemon` runs it, and scripts\atrium-autostart.ps1
in the repository registers it as a logon task.
A logon task rather than a Windows service, deliberately: a service runs in session 0
and cannot open a pseudo terminal you can attach to, which is most of what atrium is for.
Hooks: `atrium hook install` writes them into your Claude Code settings, naming the
binary the RUNNING daemon reports. Start the daemon first, then install the hooks.
